about.label: A place for possibility
about.title: From promising idea to lasting impact.
about.lead: ASF-TBI is the Technology Business Incubator of AKGEC Skills Foundation, created to help innovators take the next meaningful step.
about.description: Our incubation ecosystem is designed to bring founders, mentors, technical resources and industry perspectives together. Whether you are exploring a challenge or developing a solution, we aim to help you move forward with clarity and confidence.
about.vision: Build an inclusive, technology-driven entrepreneurial ecosystem where original ideas can grow into sustainable ventures and meaningful impact.
about.mission: Enable founders through mentorship, practical incubation support, industry collaboration and a pathway from early validation to market readiness.
objectives: Help innovators shape and validate promising startup ideas.
Provide a collaborative environment and access to incubation facilities.
Encourage entrepreneurship, experimentation and responsible innovation.
Connect founders with experienced mentors and relevant industry expertise.
Help startups explore appropriate funding and investment-readiness pathways.
Strengthen collaboration between academia, industry and entrepreneurs.

articles.title: A founder's first milestone is learning, not scaling
articles.excerpt: Why thoughtful customer discovery can help early founders build with more confidence.
articles.body:
The earliest stage of a venture is a chance to learn. Talk to the people experiencing the problem, test what you believe and keep a record of what changes your mind. Small experiments can help a team decide what to build next—and what not to build yet.

A strong first milestone is not necessarily a polished product. It is a clearer understanding of the people you want to serve and the evidence that supports your next step.

articles.title: From lab insight to a technology-led venture
articles.excerpt: A practical look at the questions that can connect technical research with real-world needs.
articles.body:
Promising research often begins with a technical insight. A venture takes shape when a team also understands who needs the solution, how it fits into their work and what evidence would make adoption worthwhile.

Early conversations with users, industry practitioners and potential collaborators can help teams connect technical possibility with practical value.

articles.title: Getting investment-ready starts before the pitch
articles.excerpt: Milestones, market learning and a clear plan help founders prepare for funding conversations.
articles.body:
A pitch is one part of an investment conversation. Founders can prepare by understanding their customers, explaining how the venture creates value and identifying the milestones that additional resources would support.

Funding opportunities differ, and every funder sets its own criteria. Careful preparation helps founders explore those options without assuming that any particular outcome is guaranteed.

application.title: Start your incubation journey
application.description: Share what you are building, who it serves and the next step you want to take. The ASF-TBI team can help you understand the application process.
eligibility: Individuals or teams with an innovative idea or early-stage venture.
A clear problem statement and a willingness to learn from potential users.
Technology-led, knowledge-led or innovation-focused concepts are welcome.
Applicants should be ready to participate in discussions and milestone reviews.
process: Review the eligibility information and prepare a concise venture overview.
Email the application team with your concept note and contact details.
The team reviews submissions and may request a conversation or additional information.
Eligible applications are evaluated against the current selection criteria.
Selected founders are contacted to discuss possible next steps and support.
documents: Founder and team profiles with contact details.
A short concept note describing the problem, proposed solution and intended users.
A prototype, demonstration or relevant supporting material, if available.
Business or validation plan and milestone outline, if available.
Organization or registration details, if already established.
evaluation: Clarity and relevance of the problem being addressed.
Innovation and potential usefulness of the proposed solution.
Understanding of users, market context and validation needs.
Founding team's ability to learn, execute and collaborate.
Alignment with available incubation support and facilities.
criteria: A meaningful problem and a credible approach to testing the solution.
Potential for a sustainable venture and a positive, responsible impact.
Founder commitment and readiness to work toward measurable milestones.
Fit with the expertise, facilities and programs available at the time.

faqs.question: Can I apply at the idea stage?
faqs.answer: Yes. Early-stage applicants can share their idea, the problem they want to address and how they plan to learn from potential users.

faqs.question: Does applying guarantee funding or incubation?
faqs.answer: No. Applications are reviewed against the current selection process, available capacity and program fit. Funding is not guaranteed.

faqs.question: What should I include in my first email?
faqs.answer: Include a short concept note, founder details, contact information and any prototype or validation material you already have.

faqs.question: How do I ask about current facilities or programs?
faqs.answer: Contact the incubation team directly. Availability and access requirements can vary.
